==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|Schedule||law}}

===Etymology===
{{inh+|en|enm|cedule}}, from {{der|en|frm|cedule}} (whence {{cog|fr|cédule}}), from {{der|en|fro|cedule}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|schedula||papyrus strip}}, diminutive of {{der|en|la|scheda}}, from {{der|en|grc|σχέδη||papyrus leaf}}, from {{der|en|grk-pro|*skʰíďďō}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro||*skid-yé-ti}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*skeyd-||to divide, split}}. {{doublet|en|cedula|cedule}}.

This word was historically pronounced {{IPAchar|/ˈsɛdjuːl/|/ˈsɛdʒuːl/}}; the pronunciations with {{IPAchar|/ʃ/}} and {{IPAchar|/sk/}} are due to the [[spelling pronunciation|spelling]] (the latter may have been reinforced by learned influence); compare {{m|en|schism}}.

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q7271585}} A [[procedural]] [[plan]], usually but not necessarily [[tabular]] in nature, indicating a [[sequence]] of [[operation]]s and the planned [[time#Noun|time]]s at which those operations are to occur. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
#: {{nearsyn|en|timeline|timetable}}
#: {{ux|en|To complete on time, we must follow the '''schedule'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|record of items-sizes-etc}} A [[serial]] [[record]] of [[item]]s, [[systematically]] arranged.
#: {{nearsyn|en|catalog|inventory|list|listing|register|registry|table}}
#: {{ux|en|The building code includes a '''schedule''' of acceptable configurations.}}
# {{lb|en|law}} A written or printed table of information, often forming an [[annex]] or [[appendix]] to a [[statute]] or other regulatory instrument, or to a legal contract. {{defdate|from 15th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''schedule''' of tribes}}
## {{senseid|en|controlled substances}} {{lb|en|US|law|often|capitalized}} One of the five divisions into which [[controlled substance]]s are classified, or the restrictions denoted by such classification. {{defdate|from 20th c.}}
##: {{ux|en|Heroin is a '''Schedule''' I drug with a high potential for abuse.}}
## {{senseid|en|controlled substances}} {{lb|en|Australia|law|medicine}} One of the nine schedules of the [[:w:Standard for the Uniform Scheduling of Medicines and Poisons|Standard for the Uniform Scheduling of Medicines and Poisons]]. {{non-gloss|Identical to the American usage above.}}
# {{lb|en|computer science}} An [[allocation]] or ordering of a set of tasks on one or several resources. {{defdate|from 20th c.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A slip of paper; a short [[note]]. {{defdate|14th|17th c.}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# To create a time-[[schedule#Noun|schedule]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[plan#Verb|plan]] (an [[activity]] or [[event]]) for a [[specific]] date or [[time]].
#: {{syn|en|make|time}}
#: {{ux|en|The next elections are '''scheduled''' on the twentieth of November.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To add (a name) to the list of those participating in an event; to [[reserve]] a place or time for.
#: {{syn|en|sign up|register#Verb|enroll|book#Verb}}
#: {{ux|en|I am '''scheduled''' for classes next month.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'll '''schedule''' you for three-o'clock then.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|Australia|medicine}} To [[admit]] (a person) to [[hospital]] as an [[involuntary]] [[patient#Noun|patient]] under a schedule of the applicable [[mental health]] law.
#: {{syn|en|section|q1=UK|commit|q2=US}}
#: {{ux|en|whether or not to '''schedule''' a patient}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|US}} To [[classify]] as a [[controlled substance]].
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Jan Hoffman|title=The Fight Over a Drug That Is Great for Horses but Horrific for Humans|date=2023-04-20|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/04/20/health/xylazine-tranq-animals.html|passage=Many harm reduction groups and drug policy experts question the long-term efficacy of '''scheduling''' xylazine.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251110132607/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/04/20/health/xylazine-tranq-animals.html|archivedate=10 November 2025}}
